text:
Jules: Hey team — our integration to Redwood streaming keeps returning a partial JSON object, last character is a trailing comma and the client errors on parse. Happening intermittently since yesterday. thread_ts=2360001111
Maya (support): Sorry you're hitting this, can you paste the raw stream bytes or curl we can repro with? Also which model and SDK?
Jules: Using node-fetch in our worker, model=gpt-neox-20b-8k, demo prompt size ~2.4k tokens. Quick repro curl attached: 
```
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxxx' \
  -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/generate
```
Maya (support): thanks. Any proxy between your worker and our API (Fastly/Cloudflare or internal LB)?
Jules: yes we have an internal envoy mesh + edge LB. We noticed if a client aborts (AbortController.abort) on reconnect, sometimes the final chunk is missing and finish_reason isn't emitted.
Kofi (eng-runtime): that pattern can expose an upstream that buffers content-length and closes connection early. Can you dump response headers from the failing run?
Jules: header dump: 
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/event-stream
content-length: 5482
transfer-encoding: chunked
x-rw-request-id: rw-9c7f2a
```
Weird: both content-length and transfer-encoding present from our side.
Priya (eng-infra): aha — envoy sometimes injects content-length when buffering responses with route configuration. If the gateway adds content-length, downstream clients may treat stream as complete when bytes==content-length, even if server intended streaming chunks afterwards. That would cause truncate + missing finish_reason.
Maya (support): good find. Jules, can you reproduce with the gateway bypassed (direct traffic to our edge) or with envoy set to chunked streaming (disable response buffering)?
Jules: Bypassing edge for a test gave a clean stream (no trailing comma). When routed through mesh we saw the partial JSON case ~3/10 requests.
Kofi (eng-runtime): can you also send us the rw request id from a failing call (we can check server logs for that id). The x-rw-request-id above looks like one. Also send the exact client-side byte sequence you received (hexdump or pasted) for the truncated stream.
Jules: sent the failing request id in DM and attached hexdump.
Maya (support): tagging eng-runtime and eng-infra for escalation. Suspect interaction: client abort/resume + upstream buffering producing content-length mismatch -> connection closed mid-event -> client parser gets partial final JSON (extra trailing comma/no finish_reason).
Kofi (eng-runtime): confirmed server produced final SSE event with finish_reason but it looks like envoy closed early for the failing x-rw-request-id. Server logs: 
```
[rw-9c7f2a] generate: final packet flushed, finish_reason="stop", bytes_sent=6120
```
Client hexdump shows only 5482 bytes (matches the content-length header the gateway set).
Priya (eng-infra): immediate mitigation: turn off response buffering on the gateway for /v1/streams/* routes or ensure Transfer-Encoding: chunked is the only indicator (remove content-length rewrite). In the long term we should add a keepalive/heartbeat SSE comment every N seconds to ensure proxies don't buffer or time out early.
Maya (support): recommended temporary workaround for customers: 1) set request header `Accept: text/event-stream` and `Connection: keep-alive`; 2) configure envoy route: `use_remote_address: false` + `x-envoy-buffering: disabled` (or equivalent) so it forwards chunked responses. 3) client-side: if you get a truncated stream, call the non-streaming completion API to fetch full output (best-effort) and correlate with rw request id for billing/consistency check.
Jules: thanks — applying buffer disable now, will report back. Quick question: billing - did we get charged for incomplete streams? We saw 1 token billed but no completion returned to client.
Maya (support): we charge on server-side emission; if the runtime emitted tokens (server-side flushes), those are billable even if client disconnected. We'll reconcile any obvious misbills if we detect server didn't finish. Please share the failing request ids and timestamps.
Jules: shared three ids in DM.
Kofi (eng-runtime): follow-up action items for eng teams: 1) add server-side periodic SSE comment heartbeat `: keepalive\n\n` every 5s for long-running streams; 2) add metric to detect when proxy-reported bytes != server bytes for same rw id; 3) add more robust client resume token header support (last-event-id) so SDKs can attempt to request tail tokens on reconnect.
Priya (eng-infra): infra action: audit envoy route configs for buffering, add test in staging that simulates abort+reconnect and assert stream integrity, and remove any layer that injects content-length for chunked responses.
Maya (support): I'll file the internal incident and link this thread. Jules, please keep this channel updated once you verify the buffer change. Also we can offer to replay logs to confirm final-message emission and issue a billing review if needed. :thumbsup:
Jules: buffer disable fixed it in my quick 30-run smoke — no partial JSONs. Thanks all, will run extended tests overnight and confirm here.
keepalive-bot: automated note: queued infra test case "stream-abort-reconnect" assigned to eng-infra, ticket #INF-824
Maya (support): closing loop here when you confirm. If it reappears, paste one failing x-rw-request-id and we'll deep dive with pcap/hexdump. :heart:
